cohort: The study involved 90 women who underwent cesarean section at a tertiary care hospital, divided into elective (n=45) and emergency (n=45) groups.
finding: Elective cesarean sections were associated with significantly shorter mean operation time, lower estimated blood loss, fewer postoperative complications, better Apgar scores, and lower rates of NICU admissions compared to emergency cesarean sections.
mod_finding: Elective cesarean sections demonstrated more favorable maternal and perinatal outcomes, including shorter operation times, less blood loss, fewer complications, better Apgar scores, and fewer neonatal admissions, compared to emergency cesarean sections.
